query: In conventional alloys, loss of toughness has long been associated with grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation. By contrast, compositionally complex high-entropy alloys can suppress rapid grain coarsening and deleterious intermetallic formation and have shown favorable strength–ductility combinations and resistance to high-temperature softening and low-temperature embrittlement. These findings do not establish what governs possible toughness degradation in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy. Under the constraint of retaining a compositionally complex alloy suitable for demanding engineering service, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why brittle behavior emerges? Specify a controlled comparison that would distinguish the hypothesis from conventional-alloy expectations, predicted observations relative to the initial baseline, its service and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification outcome.

decision.trend: Research on high-entropy alloys has focused on understanding their mechanical properties, such as strength, ductility, and toughness. Earlier studies have investigated the effects of grain size, grain boundary segregation, and deformation mechanisms on the mechanical behavior of these alloys. Recent studies have also explored the use of advanced characterization techniques, such as atom probe tomography and transmission electron microscopy, to understand the microstructural evolution and deformation mechanisms in high-entropy alloys.
decision.unsolved: The mechanisms governing toughness degradation in high-entropy alloys, particularly in single-phase alloys, remain unclear. The effects of grain boundary segregation, nanoclustering, and deformation mechanisms on toughness degradation are not well understood, and further research is needed to develop a comprehensive understanding of these phenomena.
decision.why: Atom probe tomography has been used in recent studies to investigate grain boundary segregation and nanoclustering in high-entropy alloys. This technique can provide detailed information on the microstructural evolution and deformation mechanisms in these alloys, which can help to develop a comprehensive understanding of toughness degradation. By using atom probe tomography to study the microstructure and composition of high-entropy alloys, researchers can gain insights into the mechanisms governing toughness degradation and develop strategies to improve the toughness of these alloys.
